title.quote: Patient Engagement in the Implementation of Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome Tools: The Experience of Two Early-Adopter Institutions in the Pan-Canadian Radiotherapy Patient-Reported Outcome Initiative

analysis.description: The paper discusses the experiences and lessons learned from two Canadian early adopter institutions in implementing electronic patient-reported outcomes collection in radiotherapy practice. It focuses on patient and community engagement strategies used in the development and deployment of patient engagement tools.

type.justification: The paper describes real-world implementations and experiences in two early adopter institutions.
type.quote: Aims: To share the patient and community engagement experience of two Canadian early adopter sites that implemented electronic patient-reported outcomes collection in radiotherapy practice.

name.justification: The paper focus fits into healthcare, specifically the implementation of electronic patient-reported outcomes in radiotherapy.
name.quote: Aims: To share the patient and community engagement experience of two Canadian early adopter sites that implemented electronic patient-reported outcomes collection in radiotherapy practice.

name.justification: The research involves digital health aspects like electronic patient-reported outcomes and patient engagement apps.
name.quote: With the ever-expanding availability of mobile electronic devices, greater internet access, and digital health solutions, electronic PRO (ePRO) tools have emerged with the potential to not only improve the quality of assessments but also play an important role in the development of new digital health interventions.

name.justification: The study revolves around radiotherapy practices, a key component of oncology.
name.quote: In oncology, the importance of PROs has long been recognised in the assessment of the impact of cancer and its treatments on the physical and psychosocial well-being of patients.

name.justification: The model is named directly in the context of the paper.
name.quote: A tripartite research collaboration with her radiation oncologist and a medical physicist gave rise to a tool to engage patients in their care by providing them with access to their personal health information, PROMs, and personalised educational material in a single smartphone app known as Opal (opalmedapps.com).

is_contributed.justification: The Opal Patient Portal was a primary tool developed and discussed in the scope of the research.
is_contributed.quote: The Opal patient portal project began serendipitously in 2014 when a university professor of computer science who was receiving RT for breast cancer at the MUHC offered to share her computer science expertise to help the radiation oncology department where she was being treated.

is_executed.justification: Though the model was implemented in the institutions, specific execution details like on CPU/GPU were not mentioned.

is_compared.justification: The paper does not provide a comparison of Opal with other models numerically.
